extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how postsecondary institutions must design and implement grievance procedures for sex-based harassment complaints (live hearings, live-questioning, written determinations, and appeals) under Title IX. Focused on compliance with §§106.45–106.46 and related training and procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion to use live hearings with mandatory live-questioning
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution may choose whether and under what circumstances to use a live hearing for sex-based harassment complaints involving student complainants or respondents, but must provide a live-questioning process that enables the decisionmaker to assess the credibility of parties and witnesses to the extent credibility is both in dispute and relevant to evaluating one or more allegations of sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the institution does not use a live hearing, §106.46(f)(1)(i) allows either the investigator or the decisionmaker to ask questions of parties and witnesses during individual meetings. If the investigator asks questions, the decisionmaker relies on the investigator's assessment of credibility. Institutions retain latitude to structure grievance procedures to be equitable while accommodating institutional structure and applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written grievance procedures must articulate principles for use of live hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: As required under §106.45(b)(8), the postsecondary institution's written grievance procedures must articulate consistent principles for how it will determine the types of complaints for which it will use live hearings (e.g., complaints in which both parties are students or complaints for which the maximum sanction is suspension or expulsion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient's determination regarding whether to apply certain procedures to some, but not all, complaints must be made in a manner that treats complainants and respondents equitably consistent with §106.45(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: If a live hearing is used, comply with §106.46(g) procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the postsecondary institution chooses to use a live hearing for complaints of sex-based harassment involving a student, the postsecondary institution must comply with all of the requirements for a live hearing in §106.46(g). Conversely, if it chooses not to use a live hearing, it must follow the procedures in §106.46(f)(1)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed live-questioning procedures and the options for questioning parties and witnesses to aid in evaluating allegations and assessing credibility are discussed in §106.46(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual participation requirements for live hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.46(g) permits a postsecondary institution to allow any party to participate in the live hearing virtually as long as the decisionmaker and parties can simultaneously see and hear the party or witness while that party is speaking; telephonic testimony without video is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.46(g) to require that upon the request of either party the postsecondary institution must conduct the live hearing with the parties physically present in separate locations (which can be virtual). The institution must ensure both parties have equal opportunity to speak and listen in a hybrid live hearing when one person testifies in person and the other remotely.

rubrics_metrics.name: No general authorization to "communicate in another format" except for disability accommodation
rubrics_metrics.description: The language allowing a person to 'communicat[e] in another format' was removed; the Department's intent was that alternative forms of communication are permitted only when necessary to accommodate a disability under applicable disability laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients' obligations to comply with disability laws applies to all aspects of responding to sex discrimination, including grievance procedures. Persons who do not require an accommodation would be required to speak during the hearing rather than, e.g., typing in chat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trauma-informed approaches optional (not mandated by regs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to require recipients to ensure that hearings and questioning are trauma-informed as a specific regulatory obligation, while recognizing recipients may adopt trauma-informed approaches as long as they comply with final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients that sufficiently train investigators, decisionmakers, and other persons responsible for implementing grievance procedures, as required by §106.8(d)(2), should be able to implement processes that treat complainants and respondents respectfully and fairly. Imposing specific trauma-informed obligations would interfere with recipients' flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written determination content and adequacy for appeal/judicial review (§106.46(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.46(h) mandates that a written determination must include certain key elements so parties have a thorough understanding of the investigative process and information considered; it must be adequate for the purpose of an appeal or judicial proceeding reviewing the determination regarding responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations clarify that a written determination from a postsecondary institution whether sex-based harassment occurred must include the decisionmaker's evaluation of the evidence that is 'relevant and not otherwise impermissible.' The Department declined to require an express credibility analysis or to require identification of which elements were found by the standard of proof, though such analysis would be included if relevant. Recipients are not required to specify particular remedies in the written determination—only whether remedies will be provided—to protect complainant privacy; the Title IX Coordinator coordinates remedy provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must be notified 'simultaneously' of the written determination whether sex-based harassment occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department interprets 'simultaneously' in its ordinary sense—'at the same time.' Minor, de minimis delays (e.g., a few minutes in email delivery) would not be considered noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients not required to reference code-of-conduct violations in determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require recipients to identify a violation of the recipient's code of conduct in a written determination; recipients retain the discretion to refer to provisions of their code of conduct as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.46(h) is intended to ensure the final regulations apply to a recipient's response to sex-based harassment under Title IX, not to non‑Title IX misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to offer appeals to both parties (§106.46(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution must offer both parties an appeal from a determination whether sex-based harassment occurred and from a postsecondary institution's dismissal of a complaint or any allegations therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves parity between complainant and respondent appellate rights and aligns with §106.45(b)(8) of the 2020 amendments and Clery Act principles; offering appeals equally increases likelihood of accurate outcomes and confidence in grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory bases for offering an appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must offer an appeal on the bases of: (i) procedural irregularity that affected the outcome, (ii) new evidence that was not reasonably available at the time of the determination, and (iii) Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker bias or conflict of interest that affected the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department selected these three bases because each represents an error that could indicate an inaccurate determination. The regulations balance parties' interests in review with institutional discretion to design grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: New evidence standard for appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal based on new evidence is permitted only when the new evidence 'was not reasonably available at the time of the determination or dismissal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard guards against a party withholding evidence during investigation to present on appeal. The provision does not permit appeals based on evidence that could reasonably have been presented earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient may offer additional appeal bases but must be equal
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient has discretion to offer appeals on additional bases (e.g., severity of sanction or remedy), but if it does so, both the complainant and respondent must have the opportunity to appeal on the same bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It would be unfair to permit appeals on certain bases for only one party (e.g., complainant but not respondent). Any additional appellate bases must be made equally available to both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal decisionmaker independence and impartiality requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The decisionmaker for an appeal must not be the same person who investigated the allegations or dismissed the complaint, must be free from bias and conflicts of interest, and must be trained to serve impartially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.45(d)(3)(iii) (incorporated by §106.46(a)) and §106.8(d)(2)(iii) ensure appeal decisionmakers review cases independently and are trained and free from bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of review language—'change' outcome threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations use the term 'change' (rather than 'affect' or 'impact') to describe what a party must show with respect to an enumerated appellate basis (i.e., that the basis would 'change' the outcome).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department states that using 'change' is consistent with plain language requirements and does not substantively alter application versus other terms; it is not intended to make appeals effectively impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to add appeals for simple error or against-the-weight findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require a recipient to offer appeals on the basis of simple error or that a determination is against the weight of the evidence; such issues may be considered under an allegation of bias when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law cited does not compel additional mandatory bases; where a decision is lopsided, that could support an inference of bias, which is an existing ground for appeal under §106.46(i)(1)(iii).
